historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 13.4% diverges >30% from revenue 8.0% and EPS 10.0%: book value compounded on FY2024-FY2025 peak-margin retained earnings while payout was only ~25-35%, so it is not a usable forward growth proxy. Revenue CAGR selected instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income), INR m: FY2021 28,765; FY2022 25,388; FY2023 18,821; FY2024 25,301; FY2025 31,550; FY2026 5,738. The FY2026 collapse is INR 14.8bn of intangible/in-licensing purchases plus the H2 FY26 margin drop, so the negative CAGRs are an endpoint artefact, not a trend; the FY2021-FY2025 owner-FCF CAGR was +2.3% against 9.5% revenue growth because interest income (INR 0.4bn -> 2.5bn) and capex (4.3% -> 5.6% of revenue) both grew faster than revenue. Owner FCF ran 1.2-2.7% of revenue below reported FCF; SBC itself is only 0.2% of revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: North America has reset to a ~USD 165-175m/quarter run-rate after the FY26 base-business erosion and the loss of limited-competition economics; gAdvair Diskus and gVentolin plus the first peptide launches stabilise it from H2 FY27 but do not restore the FY25 windfall. One India (48% of revenue) keeps compounding at low-double-digits on chronic therapies and consumer wellness, South Africa grows at ~1.2x market, and the mix shift lifts group EBITDA margin from 18.5% in FY27 (bottom of the maintained guidance range) back to 22% by FY31 -- the ten-year average, not the FY25 peak. The Pithampur warning letter is neither cleared nor escalated to an import alert: it continues to delay a handful of US approvals (already in the slower NA growth) without disrupting supply. In-licensing (Qilu pembrolizumab biosimilar, CTTQ HER2 ADC) keeps capex ~1pp above the historical 5%. Terminal growth of 4.5% is roughly zero real in INR.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Aug-2026 Pithampur re-inspection is classified VAI and the warning letter is lifted in FY27-28, unblocking the queued respiratory/peptide ANDAs; gAdvair takes meaningful share in a market with few generic entrants and gSymbicort/gQvar follow, taking NA back above USD 230m/quarter by FY29. India chronic growth stays 1.3x IPM, trade generics and consumer wellness scale, and operating leverage plus a richer US complex-generics mix carries EBITDA margin to 24% -- near, but still below, the FY25 25.9% peak. Capex normalises to 6% including licensing, and terminal growth of 5% reflects a company still outgrowing nominal GDP modestly at maturity.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Pithampur classification comes back OAI and the facility goes to import alert or needs a multi-year remediation, blocking new US approvals and forcing site transfers for part of the respiratory portfolio; US base-business pricing keeps eroding at high-single digits with no launch offsets, so NA keeps shrinking in FY27-28. In India, the pending NPPA litigation and an NLEM expansion cap pricing on a quarter of the domestic portfolio, slowing One India to high-single digits. FY27 EBITDA margin lands at 17.5%, below the guidance floor, and settles at 19% -- the FY2017-FY2020 range -- as R&D at ~6% of revenue and remediation costs are sticky. Revenue growth of 4-5% is barely above INR inflation, and terminal growth is 4%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Cipla as a stream of owner free cash flow in INR, discounted at an INR cost of equity, with the FY2024-FY2026 peak margins treated as a windfall rather than a run-rate and the FY2026 FCF trough treated as capex lumpiness rather than a collapse. The three scenarios differ on the two axes that actually drive the equity -- US regulatory status at Pithampur / North America run-rate, and the pace of margin recovery toward the ten-year average -- and are weighted 25/50/25 to reflect a live regulatory binary. Net cash of INR 98bn (about 8% of market cap) is added to enterprise value with its interest income stripped from the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Pithampur USFDA classification (pending from the Aug-2026 re-inspection): an import alert or prolonged OAI status would push outcomes toward the bear path; a VAI/closeout would validate the bull path's approval cadence

North America run-rate: each USD 10m/quarter of NA revenue is roughly 1.3% of group revenue at ~25% incremental margin, so the FY27-FY28 recovery assumption is the largest near-term driver of the base case
Margin recovery pace: the base case assumes 22% by FY31; every 1pp of mature EBITDA margin is roughly INR 40-45/share of value at 10.5% WACC
Discount rate and terminal growth in INR: value is terminal-heavy, and the WACC x g grid should be read with INR inflation in mind -- 4.5% terminal growth is ~zero real
Working-capital intensity (NWC ~34% of revenue) and in-licensing capex: if biosimilar deal milestones recur annually, capex may stay nearer 7% than 6.5%
India price controls: an NLEM/NPPA expansion would hit the highest-margin segment directly

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (NSE regular close) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1165.7-1539.7; to be refreshed by scripts/refresh_price.py
data_sources.financials: CIPLA.NS_Metrics.csv (consolidated Ind AS, INR millions converted from crores, FY2016-FY2026 annual plus quarters to Q2 FY2027); CIPLA.NS_Annual_FY2026.txt for the net-debt note, lease principal, diluted shares and cash taxes; CIPLA.NS_Presentation_Q2-FY2027.txt for the Sep-2026 balance sheet, North America USD revenue and FY27 EBITDA margin guidance
data_sources.qualitative: CIPLA.NS_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): Pithampur warning letter and Aug-2026 Form 483, Goa Form 483, NLEM/NPPA exposure, Q2 FY27 results, CLSA downgrade to Hold (INR 1,580), consensus target ~INR 1,500

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 consolidated cash flow statement, share-based payment expense INR 59.05 crore (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp); no equity-award tax line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year), so the add-back is the full cost
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares FY2026, 80,82,47,427 (Annual FY2026 txt line 23787); shares on issue 80,77,82,631 at 31 Mar 2026. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; ESOP dilution is ~0.05%/yr and there is no non-SBC issuance. Cipla has never repurchased shares, so the flat count is a modelling convention, not funded by buybacks -- immaterial at 0.2% SBC.
inputs.net_debt_note: Sep-2026 Q2 FY27 investor presentation (balance sheet slide): cash and cash equivalents INR 10,522 crore (includes current investments, fixed deposits and margin deposits, excludes unclaimed dividend) less total debt INR 699 crore (includes lease liabilities and borrowings) = net cash INR 9,823 crore = INR 98,230m. FY2026 annual net-debt note (line 23714) showed net cash INR 9,305.70 crore at 31 Mar 2026 on the same definition. Interest income (INR 2,279m FY2026) is stripped from the FCF base because the cash pile is added to EV; the 'other income' line also carries fair-value gains on current investments, which are likewise excluded from EBITDA.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR, the currency of the flows. 10-year G-sec ~6.5% (Nov-2026), India equity risk premium ~6%, Cipla beta ~0.6 (defensive domestic pharma; low-beta large cap) gives CAPM cost of equity ~10.1%; rounded up to 10.5% as the house margin. Debt is <1% of capital so WACC = cost of equity. Same WACC in all three scenarios: regulatory and US-pricing risk is charged in the flows and the probability weights, not stacked into the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. Lease liabilities (INR ~1.4bn) are inside the company's own total-debt figure used in net_debt; lease principal (INR 1,078m FY2026, line 25030) is NOT deducted from the flows. Ongoing lease-asset renewal is charged through capex_pct instead: +0.4pp of revenue (FY2026 principal + interest INR 1,361m / revenue 281,626m = 0.48%) is folded into every scenario's capex path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (Cipla Maroc, Cipla Medpro minorities; NCI share of profit INR -26 crore in Q2 FY27, +0.14% of FY2026 profit). No deduction made; flows are treated as fully attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (scenario-weighted), via dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US' -- Cipla is a profitable branded/generic pharma manufacturer, not a bank, REIT, LIC, holdco or distressed shell; adaptations file read for INR WACC, leases, NCI, working-capital sign. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). PEAK-MARGIN GUARD: FY2025 EBITDA margin of 25.9% and FY2024 24.2% were lifted by US respiratory/complex-generic windfalls (gAlbuterol share gains, Lanreotide, limited-competition launches); the 10-year FY2017-FY2026 average is 21.1% and FY2021-2023 ran 21-22.5%. H1 FY27 printed 16.7% / 18.7% (17.8% blended) on a ~25% YoY USD fall in North America revenue (USD 162m / 172m vs 226m / 233m), and management guides FY27 at 18.5-20%. The base case therefore starts FY27 at 18.5% (low end of guidance, since H1 is below the range) and recovers to 22% by FY31 -- the long-run average plus a modest One-India mix benefit -- not to the FY2025 peak. FY2026 reported FCF (INR 8.6bn) is depressed by INR 14.8bn of intangible purchases (in-licensing); capex is normalised at 6.5% of revenue (PPE ~5% + ongoing licensing ~1% + 0.4pp lease renewal) after two elevated years at 6.9%, versus the FY2017-FY2025 average of ~5.0%. Working capital consumes cash on growth: inventory + receivables - payables was INR 9,512 crore at Sep-2026 (~34% of TTM revenue), and FY2024-FY2026 OCF shortfalls against EBITDA less cash tax imply 17-26% of the revenue increase, so wc_capture is -22%. Cash tax rate 26.5% sits between the 25.9% FY2026 effective rate and the ~30% cash-paid/PBT ratio (advance-tax timing). Terminal growth 4.5% is a nominal INR figure (RBI inflation target 4%; nominal GDP ~10%), i.e. roughly zero real growth at maturity; Gordon at 10.5%/4.5% implies 17.4x terminal FCF, inside the 18x cap. Hurdle rate 15% is the house default, applied in INR. Price field is a placeholder from the Yahoo chart API and will be refreshed by scripts/refresh_price.py.

base.growth_note: FY27 +2%: H1 FY27 revenue was flat YoY (INR 145,230m vs 145,460m) with One India +12% offsetting North America -25% in USD; H2 laps the already-weak H2 FY26 (NA USD 167m/155m) and gets gAdvair Diskus and gVentolin. FY28-FY30 7-8% as NA stabilises and India chronic growth (~11% CLSA) carries the mix, fading to 5% by FY36.
base.margin_note: FY27 18.5% = low end of the maintained 18.5-20% guidance (H1 blended 17.8% requires ~19.2% in H2 to reach it). Recovery to 22% by FY31 = FY2017-FY2026 average 21.1% plus ~1pp One-India mix shift; deliberately below the FY2024-FY2025 24-26% windfall years.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved off the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear is raised because Cipla has a live single-regulator dependency: the Pithampur site has been under a USFDA warning letter since Nov-2023, the Aug-2026 re-inspection produced a fresh seven-observation Form 483 whose classification is still pending, and the plant supplies the US respiratory portfolio -- an import alert is a real, dated, binary event rather than generic pessimism; H1 FY27 also printed below the guidance range that the base case leans on. Bull is cut to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once -- a clean Pithampur classification, multiple complex-generic launches (gAdvair, gSymbicort, peptides) gaining share, and margin recovery to 24% -- while the FY25 peak those margins approach was itself a windfall.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
